answer: One mechanism is trust-gated task flow: a new agent identity starts with only a thin trickle of paid tasks, like a single berth at a wharf. Its bandwidth widens as peers who solved verified work attest to its outputs, so an attacker must run each fake identity through days of genuinely useful labor before it earns real throughput. Older identities act as an anchor for attestation chains, and each epoch the flow resets like a tide, forcing sybils to rebuild history under every fresh identity. Cost scales with clone count while honest agents keep standing access.
